newsitem.title: INDIA: India reducing edible oil imports after new crop.
newsitem.headline: India reducing edible oil imports after new crop.

text.p: India, a large edible oil importer, is expected to scale down purchases in the coming months following good oilseed crop arrivals and adequate palm olein stocks, industry officials said on Wednesday.
"New crop arrivals are gathering momentum and we have sufficient inventories of imported palm olein," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters by telephone.
"Therefore imports in the coming three to four months will drop substantially," he said.
Shah said India imported an average 80,000 to 100,000 tonnes of palm olein per month during September, October and November.
In the next three to four months India will import a maximum of 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes of palm olein per month, Shah said.
Palm olein accounts for nearly 80 percent of India's annual edible oil imports.
"Indian importers are not booking any large commitments," Shah said.
Demand for edible oil almost triples during the Hindu festival months of September to November when domestic supplies are at their tightest due to the end of the season.

"In December, January, and February, my estimate will be no more than around 50,000 tonnes of edible oil imports per month," G.K. Sood, chief executive of Vanaspati Manufacturers Association of India, told Reuters.
India in 1995/96 (November to October) imported about 1.25 million tonnes of edible oil, of which nearly one million tonnes was palm olein.
Industry officials said domestic prices had fallen substantially and were expected to stabilise in the coming months as arrivals increase.
"Around 200,000 bags (one bag = 70 kg) of soybean seed in Madhya Pradesh and about 100,000 bags of groundnut in Gujarat are arriving per day," Shah said.
Central Madhya Pradesh state contributes nearly 80 percent to the country's soybean production and western Gujarat state provides some 35 percent of India's groundnut output.

Shah said groundnut oil was currently at 35,000 rupees a tonne in the domestic markets compared to 40,000 a tonne at the same time last year. Soybean oil was quoted at 28,000 rupees a tonne against 33,000 rupees a tonne last November.
Industry officials said India's 1996/97 winter production of oilseeds was projected at 11.4 million tonnes, the same as last year, and edible oil output about 3.6 million tonnes.
India produces two oilseed crops annually, getting the bulk of the output from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop is done during July and the harvest begins in October.
